<a name="SaleLineItemV10"></a>
## type [SaleLineItemV10](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L681-L736>)

A single line of a sale.

The envelope \(id, type, name, quantity, unit\_of\_measure, price\) is stable and type\-agnostic: any consumer can render and total a line from these fields alone. Type\-specific data is in \`features\`. There is no per\-type object and no discriminator, so a new item type does not change this schema.

```go
type SaleLineItemV10 struct {
    // Categories the line belongs to. A shared optional structure available to any
    // line; not a per-type field.
    // Max items: 1000
    Categories []CategoryV10 `json:"categories,omitempty"`
    // Named, typed, type-specific data. New item types add their data here as
    // features instead of new schema variants. See `Feature` for per-type examples.
    // Max items: 100
    Features []FeatureV10 `json:"features,omitempty"`
    // Stable identifier of the line within the sale. Used for linking (e.g. deposits).
    // Max length: 100
    ID  string `json:"id"`
    // Modifiers customise a line (e.g. "oat milk" on a cappuccino). A shared
    // optional structure available to any line; not a per-type field.
    // Max items: 50
    Modifiers []ModifierItem `json:"modifiers,omitempty"`
    // Display name of the line.
    // Max length: 250
    Name string `json:"name"`
    // Optional free-text note attached to the line, visible on receipts.
    // Max length: 300
    Note *string `json:"note,omitempty"`
    // Pricing for a single line, valid for every item type.
    //
    // Merges the standard amounts (with tax breakdown) and the final amounts (after
    // discounts/modifiers).
    //
    // Totals and tax amounts can be negative for return-like operations (for example
    // a deposit with `operation_type` = `RETURN`).
    Price LineItemPriceV10 `json:"price"`
    // The numerical value representing the quantity in the specified unit.
    // Format: double
    // Min: 0
    Quantity float64 `json:"quantity"`
    // Outward identifiers and links for a line, kept in one place rather than scattered
    // per item type.
    References *ItemReferencesV10 `json:"references,omitempty"`
    // The type of service for this line.
    ServiceType *SaleLineItemV10ServiceType `json:"service_type,omitempty"`
    // Classifies a sale line. Not a schema subclass.
    //
    // Known values: `CATALOG`, `DEPOSIT`, `GIFT_CARD`, `CUSTOM`, `FEE`.
    //
    // `FEE` lines represent merchant-charged fees on the sale (e.g. shipping, service
    // charge, surcharge, cancellation). They participate in sale totals like any other
    // line; type-specific data is carried in `features` (see `Feature` for the
    // conventional feature keys).
    //
    // This is intentionally an open string, NOT a closed enum: new values are added
    // over time as pure data and consumers MUST tolerate unknown values, rendering the
    // line from the generic envelope (name, quantity, price, taxes) and reading any
    // extra information from `features`.
    Type string `json:"type"`
    // The unit of measure of the item.
    UnitOfMeasure UnitOfMeasure `json:"unit_of_measure"`
}
```


<a name="SalePriceV10"></a>
## type [SalePriceV10](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L762-L783>)

Sale\-level pricing aggregate, parallel to \`LineItemPrice\` on each \`SaleLineItem\`.

Line\-level breakdown \(unit price, line discounts, per\-line taxes\) lives on \`items\[\].price\`. This object holds the rolled\-up totals and cart\-level adjustments that consumers use for receipts and payment reconciliation.

```go
type SalePriceV10 struct {
    // Discounts applied at cart level. Item-level discounts remain on
    // `items[].price.discounts`.
    // Max items: 1000
    CartDiscounts []DiscountLine `json:"cart_discounts,omitempty"`
    // Final gross total for the sale: sum of `items[].price.total_gross_amount_final`
    // after cart-level discounts (tips excluded).
    // Same value as search `total_amount`, in minor units according to `Sale.currency.scale`.
    // Payment amounts include tips and can therefore differ from this gross total.
    // Format: int64
    GrossAmount int64 `json:"gross_amount"`
    // Final net total for the sale: sum of `items[].price.total_net_amount_final`
    // after cart-level discounts (tips excluded).
    // In minor units according to `Sale.currency.scale`.
    // Format: int64
    NetAmount int64 `json:"net_amount"`
    // Tax lines aggregated across the sale (after cart-level discounts).
    // Per-line tax detail remains on `items[].price.taxes` / `taxes_final`.
    // Min items: 1
    // Max items: 1000
    Taxes []TaxLine `json:"taxes"`
}
```

<a name="SaleSearchRequest"></a>
## type [SaleSearchRequest](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L818-L840>)

Filter and pagination criteria for \`POST /sales/search\`. Filters from different categories stack with \*\*logical AND\*\*; multiple values in one array field stack with \*\*logical OR\*\*. Results cover the merchant’s \*\*last two years\*\* of sales \(narrow further with \`start\_date\` / \`end\_date\`\). Results are sorted \*\*newest first\*\* by sale close date.

```go
type SaleSearchRequest struct {
    // Sale created **on or before** this instant (inclusive).
    EndDate *time.Time `json:"end_date,omitempty"`
    // Maximum number of results per page.
    // Default: 10
    // Min: 1
    // Max: 25
    PaginationLimit *int `json:"pagination_limit,omitempty"`
    // Opaque pagination token from a previous search response. Not interchangeable with tokens
    // from `GET /sales`.
    PaginationToken *string `json:"pagination_token,omitempty"`
    // Filters rows by payment outcome. Multiple values match any of them (**OR**). The search
    // row does not echo this value.
    PaymentStatuses []PaymentStatusFilterV10 `json:"payment_statuses,omitempty"`
    // Filters rows by sale lifecycle (`state`). Multiple values match any of them (**OR**).
    // Uses the same values as `Sale.state`. Non-finalised sales are never returned; only
    // fully-paid sales.
    SaleStatuses []SaleStateV10 `json:"sale_statuses,omitempty"`
    // Sales channel filter. Multiple values match any of them (**OR**).
    SalesChannels []SalesChannelFilterV10 `json:"sales_channels,omitempty"`
    // Sale created **on or after** this instant (inclusive).
    StartDate *time.Time `json:"start_date,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="SalesActivityCurrency"></a>
## type [SalesActivityCurrency](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L883-L894>)

The currency of the sale.

```go
type SalesActivityCurrency struct {
    // 3-letter currency code as defined by ISO-4217.
    // Format: iso-4217
    // Min length: 3
    // Max length: 3
    Code string `json:"code"`
    // The scaling factor to apply to the value to arrive at the currency's major unit. Providing a scale mitigates changes
    // to the minor unit over time, for example due to inflation. For example, if `scale` is denoted by `s` and
    // `value` is denoted by  `v` is the value, then one arrives at the major currency value by calculating `v
    // / 10^s`.
    Scale int `json:"scale"`
}
```


<a name="SalesClient.ListSalesV10"></a>
### func \(\*SalesClient\) [ListSalesV10](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L1057>)

```go
func (c *SalesClient) ListSalesV10(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, params SalesListSalesV10Params) (*SalePage, error)
```

Returns a paginated list of \`Sale\` objects. Results are sorted \*\*newest first\*\* by the \*\*newest event\*\* recorded for each sale. Pagination tokens follow that order.

Covers the merchant’s \*\*last two years\*\* of sales. Non\-finalised sales are never returned; only fully\-paid sales. Use \`POST /sales/search\` for filtered queries.

<a name="SalesClient.SearchSalesV10"></a>
### func \(\*SalesClient\) [SearchSalesV10](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L1016>)

```go
func (c *SalesClient) SearchSalesV10(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, body SalesSearchSalesV10Params) (*SaleSearchResponse, error)
```

Returns a paginated list of \`SaleSearchItem\` rows matching filter criteria. Results are sorted \*\*newest first\*\* by \*\*sale close date\*\*.

Filters from different categories stack with \*\*logical AND\*\*; multiple values in one array field stack with \*\*logical OR\*\*. Results cover the merchant’s \*\*last two years\*\* of sales \(narrow further with \`start\_date\` / \`end\_date\`\). Pagination tokens are not interchangeable with \`GET /sales\`.

<a name="TaxMode"></a>
## type [TaxMode](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/sales.go#L949>)

The tax mode used by merchant for displaying prices and calculating taxes: \- NO\_TAX: The prices don't contain any taxes, merchant don't report taxes \- GROSS: The prices used by merchant already include taxes \(common in EU\), the tax is calculated from the gross price \- NET: The prices used by merchant don't include taxes \(common in US\), the tax is calculated from the net price Since tax values can be different for the same net price depending if the tax was calculated from gross or net price, this info is necessary to be able to reconcile tax calculations.

```go
type TaxMode string
```

```go

    TaxModeGross TaxMode = "GROSS"
    TaxModeNet   TaxMode = "NET"
    TaxModeNoTax TaxMode = "NO_TAX"
)
```

<a name="TokensClient"></a>
## type [TokensClient](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/tokens.go#L66-L68>)

TokensClient provides access to the Tokens API.

Merchant tokens let your application accept card\-present payments with SumUp SDKs that support token\-based authentication. Use them when you want users to sign in to your application with your own authentication, then accept payments for a SumUp merchant account.

Create tokens on your backend using one of the \[supported authentication methods\]\(https://developer.sumup.com/api/authentication\). Keep your authentication credentials on your backend. Return only the short\-lived merchant token to your application and pass its \`access\_token\` to the SDK.

Before returning a token, authenticate the user in your application and check that they can accept payments for the requested merchant account. A merchant token is limited to that account and the requested actions, and does not grant permissions beyond those of the identity that created it.

Tokens expire 15 minutes after creation. Use \`expires\_in\` to determine the remaining lifetime and create a new token when needed. This endpoint does not return a refresh token. Treat merchant tokens as secrets: send them over HTTPS and keep them out of URLs, logs, and source code.

```go
type TokensClient struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="NewTokensClient"></a>
### func [NewTokensClient](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/tokens.go#L70>)

```go
func NewTokensClient(c *client.Client) *TokensClient
```



<a name="TokensClient.Create"></a>
### func \(\*TokensClient\) [Create](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/tokens.go#L82>)

```go
func (c *TokensClient) Create(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, body TokensCreateParams) (*Token, error)
```

Creates a short\-lived token for the merchant account identified by \`merchant\_code\` and the requested actions.

Call this endpoint from your backend using a \[supported authentication method\]\(https://developer.sumup.com/api/authentication\). You must have access to the merchant account. Before returning the token, check that the user signed in to your application is allowed to accept payments for that account.

Pass the returned \`access\_token\` to the SDK. The token expires 15 minutes after creation; use \`expires\_in\` for its remaining lifetime. To continue after it expires, create a new token through this endpoint.

<a name="TransactionBase"></a>
## type [TransactionBase](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/shared.go#L274-L301>)

Core details shared by transaction resources.

```go
type TransactionBase struct {
    // Total amount of the transaction in major units of `currency`, for example `10.1` for EUR 10.10.
    Amount *float32 `json:"amount,omitempty"`
    // Three-letter [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code of the amount.
    Currency *Currency `json:"currency,omitempty"`
    // Unique identifier of the transaction.
    ID  *string `json:"id,omitempty"`
    // Number of installments for a deferred payment.
    // Min: 1
    InstallmentsCount *int `json:"installments_count,omitempty"`
    // Payment category recorded on a transaction, for example `POS` for a point-of-sale card payment, `ECOM` for
    // an online card payment, or `RECURRING` for a recurring card payment. These reporting values are separate from
    // the lowercase `payment_type` values used to process checkouts.
    PaymentType *PaymentType `json:"payment_type,omitempty"`
    // Current status of the transaction.
    //
    // - `PENDING`: The transaction has been created but its final outcome is not known yet.
    // - `SUCCESSFUL`: The transaction completed successfully.
    // - `CANCELLED`: The transaction was cancelled or otherwise reversed before completion.
    // - `FAILED`: The transaction attempt did not complete successfully.
    // - `REFUNDED`: The transaction was refunded in full or in part.
    Status *TransactionStatus `json:"status,omitempty"`
    // The timestamp of when the transaction was created.
    Timestamp *time.Time `json:"timestamp,omitempty"`
    // SumUp transaction code, for example `TEENSK4W2K`. Use it to look up the transaction with the `transaction_code` query
    // parameter. This is separate from the transaction's `id` and the card issuer's `auth_code`.
    TransactionCode *string `json:"transaction_code,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="TransactionEvent"></a>
## type [TransactionEvent](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L158-L203>)

Detailed information about a transaction event.

```go
type TransactionEvent struct {
    // Amount of the event in major units of the associated transaction's currency.
    // Format: decimal
    Amount *float64 `json:"amount,omitempty"`
    // Date when the transaction event occurred.
    // Format: date
    Date *datetime.Date `json:"date,omitempty"`
    // Date when the transaction event is due to occur.
    // Format: date
    DueDate *datetime.Date `json:"due_date,omitempty"`
    // Financial event associated with a transaction.
    //
    // - `PAYOUT`: Funds from the transaction being prepared for or included in a merchant payout. Check the event
    // status to determine whether they have been paid out.
    // - `REFUND`: Money returned to the payer.
    // - `CHARGE_BACK`: A reversal of the payment following a chargeback.
    // - `PAYOUT_DEDUCTION`: An amount deducted from a merchant payout, for example to cover a refund or chargeback.
    EventType *TransactionEventType `json:"event_type,omitempty"`
    // Numeric identifier of a transaction event. Use it as `tx_event_id` when requesting receipt details for a
    // specific event. This is separate from the transaction ID and the transaction history pagination references.
    // Format: int64
    ID  *int64 `json:"id,omitempty"`
    // Consecutive number of the installment that is paid. Applicable only to payout events, i.e. `event_type =
    // PAYOUT`.
    InstallmentNumber *int `json:"installment_number,omitempty"`
    // Status of the transaction event.
    //
    // Not every value is used for every event type.
    //
    // - `PENDING`: The event has been created but is not final yet. Used for events that are still being processed and
    // whose final outcome is not known yet.
    // - `SCHEDULED`: The event is planned for a future payout cycle but has not been executed yet. This applies to
    // payout events before money is actually sent out.
    // - `RECONCILED`: The underlying payment has been matched with settlement data and is ready to continue through
    // payout processing, but the funds have not been paid out yet. This applies to payout events.
    // - `PAID_OUT`: The payout event has been completed and the funds were included in a merchant payout.
    // - `REFUNDED`: A refund event has been accepted and recorded in the refund flow. This is the status returned for
    // refund events once the transaction amount is being or has been returned to the payer.
    // - `SUCCESSFUL`: The event completed successfully. Use this as the generic terminal success status for event
    // types that do not expose a more specific business outcome such as `PAID_OUT` or `REFUNDED`.
    // - `FAILED`: The event could not be completed. Typical examples are a payout that could not be executed or
    // an event that was rejected during processing.
    Status *TransactionEventStatus `json:"status,omitempty"`
    // Date and time of the transaction event.
    Timestamp *time.Time `json:"timestamp,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="TransactionEventStatus"></a>
## type [TransactionEventStatus](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/shared.go#L336>)

Status of the transaction event.

Not every value is used for every event type.

\- \`PENDING\`: The event has been created but is not final yet. Used for events that are still being processed and whose final outcome is not known yet. \- \`SCHEDULED\`: The event is planned for a future payout cycle but has not been executed yet. This applies to payout events before money is actually sent out. \- \`RECONCILED\`: The underlying payment has been matched with settlement data and is ready to continue through payout processing, but the funds have not been paid out yet. This applies to payout events. \- \`PAID\_OUT\`: The payout event has been completed and the funds were included in a merchant payout. \- \`REFUNDED\`: A refund event has been accepted and recorded in the refund flow. This is the status returned for refund events once the transaction amount is being or has been returned to the payer. \- \`SUCCESSFUL\`: The event completed successfully. Use this as the generic terminal success status for event types that do not expose a more specific business outcome such as \`PAID\_OUT\` or \`REFUNDED\`. \- \`FAILED\`: The event could not be completed. Typical examples are a payout that could not be executed or an event that was rejected during processing.

```go
type TransactionEventStatus string
```

<a name="TransactionEventStatusFailed"></a>

```go
const (
    TransactionEventStatusFailed     TransactionEventStatus = "FAILED"
    TransactionEventStatusPaidOut    TransactionEventStatus = "PAID_OUT"
    TransactionEventStatusPending    TransactionEventStatus = "PENDING"
    TransactionEventStatusReconciled TransactionEventStatus = "RECONCILED"
    TransactionEventStatusRefunded   TransactionEventStatus = "REFUNDED"
    TransactionEventStatusScheduled  TransactionEventStatus = "SCHEDULED"
    TransactionEventStatusSuccessful TransactionEventStatus = "SUCCESSFUL"
)
```

Financial event associated with a transaction.

Check the event status to determine whether they have been paid out. \- \`REFUND\`: Money returned to the payer. \- \`CHARGE\_BACK\`: A reversal of the payment following a chargeback. \- \`PAYOUT\_DEDUCTION\`: An amount deducted from a merchant payout, for example to cover a refund or chargeback.

```go
type TransactionFull struct {
    // Total amount of the transaction in major units of `currency`, for example `10.1` for EUR 10.10.
    Amount *float32 `json:"amount,omitempty"`

    DeviceInfo *Device `json:"device_info,omitempty"`

    // How the payment details were captured, for example `CHIP` or `CONTACTLESS` for card-present payments and
    // `CUSTOMER_ENTRY` for card details entered by the payer. For wallet and alternative payment methods, this can
    // identify the method, such as `APPLE_PAY` or `BLIK`.
    EntryMode *EntryMode `json:"entry_mode,omitempty"`
    // Compact list of events related to the transaction.

    // Total SumUp transaction fee in major units of the transaction's currency.

    // External transaction identifier supplied by the client.
    ForeignTransactionID *string `json:"foreign_transaction_id,omitempty"`
    // Indication of the precision of the geographical position received from the payment terminal.

    // Unique identifier of the transaction.

    // Number of installments for a deferred payment.

    // Latitude value from the coordinates of the payment location (as received from the payment terminal reader).

    // Max: 90

    // List of hyperlinks for accessing related resources.
    Links []Link `json:"links,omitempty"`
    // Local timestamp of when the transaction was created.
    LocalTime *time.Time `json:"local_time,omitempty"`
    // Details of the payment location as received from the payment terminal.
    Location *TransactionFullLocation `json:"location,omitempty"`
    // Longitude value from the coordinates of the payment location (as received from the payment terminal reader).
    // Min: -180
    // Max: 180
    Lon *float32 `json:"lon,omitempty"`
    // Unique code of the registered merchant to whom the payment is made.
    MerchantCode *string `json:"merchant_code,omitempty"`
    // Internal SumUp identifier of the merchant.
    // Format: int64
    MerchantID *int64 `json:"merchant_id,omitempty"`
    // Payment category recorded on a transaction, for example `POS` for a point-of-sale card payment, `ECOM` for
    // an online card payment, or `RECURRING` for a recurring card payment. These reporting values are separate from
    // the lowercase `payment_type` values used to process checkouts.
    PaymentType *PaymentType `json:"payment_type,omitempty"`
    // The date of the payout.
    // Format: date
    PayoutDate *datetime.Date `json:"payout_date,omitempty"`
    // Payout plan of the registered user at the time when the transaction was made.
    PayoutPlan *TransactionFullPayoutPlan `json:"payout_plan,omitempty"`
    // Payout type for the transaction.
    PayoutType *TransactionFullPayoutType `json:"payout_type,omitempty"`
    // Number of payouts that are made to the registered user specified in the `user` property.
    PayoutsReceived *int `json:"payouts_received,omitempty"`
    // Total number of payouts to the registered user specified in the `user` property.
    PayoutsTotal *int `json:"payouts_total,omitempty"`
    // Whether the transaction was processed as credit or debit.
    ProcessAs *TransactionFullProcessA `json:"process_as,omitempty"`
    // Short description of the payment. The value is taken from the `description` property of the related checkout resource.

    // Simple name of the payment type.

    // High-level status of the transaction from the merchant's perspective.

    // - `PENDING`: The payment has been initiated and is still being processed. A final outcome is not available yet.
    //
    // - `SUCCESSFUL`: The payment was completed successfully.
    // - `PAID_OUT`: The payment was completed successfully and the funds have already been included in a payout to

    // - `REFUNDED`: The payment was refunded in full or in part.
```

<a name="TransactionsClient"></a>
## type [TransactionsClient](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L761-L763>)

TransactionsClient provides access to the Transactions API.

Transactions represent completed or attempted payment operations processed for a merchant account. A transaction contains the core payment result, such as the amount, currency, payment method, creation time, and current high\-level status.

In addition to the main payment outcome, a transaction can contain related events that describe what happened after the original payment attempt. These events provide visibility into the financial lifecycle of the transaction, for example: \- \`PAYOUT\`: the payment being prepared for payout or included in a payout to the merchant \- \`REFUND\`: money returned to the payer \- \`CHARGE\_BACK\`: money reversed after the original payment \- \`PAYOUT\_DEDUCTION\`: an amount deducted from a payout to cover a refund or chargeback

From an integrator's perspective, transactions are the authoritative record of payment outcomes. Use this tag to: \- list transactions for reporting, reconciliation, and customer support workflows \- retrieve a single transaction when you need the latest payment details \- inspect \`simple\_status\` for the current merchant\-facing outcome of the payment \- inspect \`events\` or \`transaction\_events\` when you need refund, payout, or chargeback history

Typical workflow: \- create and process payments through the Checkouts endpoints \- use the Transactions endpoints to read the resulting payment records \- use the returned statuses and events to update your own order, accounting, or support systems

```go
type TransactionsClient struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```




<a name="TransactionsClient.Get"></a>
### func \(\*TransactionsClient\) [Get](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L811>)

```go
func (c *TransactionsClient) Get(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, params TransactionsGetParams) (*TransactionFull, error)
```

Retrieves the full details of an identified transaction. The transaction resource is identified by a query parameter and \*one\* of following parameters is required: \- \`id\` \- \`transaction\_code\` \- \`foreign\_transaction\_id\` \- \`client\_transaction\_id\`

<a name="TransactionsClient.List"></a>
### func \(\*TransactionsClient\) [List](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L775>)

```go
func (c *TransactionsClient) List(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, params TransactionsListParams) (*TransactionsListResponse, error)
```

Lists transaction history for the merchant, with optional filters for payment type, status, and date range. The response contains the current page in \`items\` and pagination query strings in \`links\`.

To request another page, use the query string from the relevant link's \`href\` with this history endpoint. Use \`changes\_since\` when retrieving transactions modified since a previous synchronization, including transactions created earlier whose status has changed.

<a name="TransactionsClient.Refund"></a>
### func \(\*TransactionsClient\) [Refund](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L846>)

```go
func (c *TransactionsClient) Refund(ctx context.Context, merchantCode string, transactionID string, body TransactionsRefundParams) (*TransactionsRefundResponse, error)
```

Refunds a transaction identified by its SumUp transaction ID. Omit the request body to request a full refund, or provide \`amount\` for a partial refund in the transaction's currency.

Retrieve the transaction afterwards to inspect its refunded amount and refund events. The transaction must be eligible for a refund; see the error responses for invalid amounts, permissions, and processing failures.

<a name="TransactionsListParams"></a>
## type [TransactionsListParams](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/transactions.go#L593-L629>)

TransactionsListParams are query parameters for ListTransactionsV2.1.

```go
type TransactionsListParams struct {
    // Filters the results by the latest modification time of resources and returns only transactions that are modified
    // *at or after* the specified timestamp (in [ISO8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format).
    ChangesSince *time.Time
    // Filters the returned results by the specified list of entry modes.
    EntryModes []EntryMode
    // Maximum number of transactions per page. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to `10` when omitted; a page
    // can contain fewer results.
    Limit *int
    // Pagination reference that returns results before the specified reference. Use the value from a returned pagination
    // link rather than constructing it yourself. This parameter takes precedence over `newest_time` when both are
    // provided.
    NewestRef *string
    // Filters the results by the creation time of resources and returns only transactions that are created *before*
    // the specified timestamp (in [ISO8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format).
    NewestTime *time.Time
    // Pagination reference that returns results after the specified reference. Use the value from a returned pagination
    // link rather than constructing it yourself. This parameter takes precedence over `oldest_time` when both are
    // provided.
    OldestRef *string
    // Filters the results by the creation time of resources and returns only transactions that are created *at
    // or after* the specified timestamp (in [ISO8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format).
    OldestTime *time.Time
    // Sort direction for the transaction history. Use `ascending` or `descending`; the default is `ascending`.
    Order *TransactionsListOrder
    // Filters the returned results by the specified list of payment types used for the transactions.
    PaymentTypes []PaymentType
    // Filters transactions by the listed final statuses. For multiple values, repeat the query parameter, for example
    // `statuses[]=SUCCESSFUL&statuses[]=REFUNDED`.
    Statuses []TransactionsListStatusesItem
    // Retrieves the transaction resource with the specified transaction code.
    TransactionCode *string
    // Filters the returned results by the specified list of transaction types.
    Types []TransactionsListTypesItem
    // Filters transactions by user email. For multiple values, repeat the query parameter, for example `users[]=first@example.com&users[]=second@example.com`.
    Users []string
}
```

<a name="TypedEvent"></a>
## type [TypedEvent](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/events.go#L27-L38>)

TypedEvent contains common notification fields and fetches its resource as T. Concrete event types are generated from the OpenAPI webhooks. Notifications may be retried or arrive out of order: make processing idempotent and fetch the latest resource when reconciling local state.

```go
type TypedEvent[T any] struct {

    // ID identifies this notification, including across retries.
    ID  string `json:"id"`
    // Type is the wire event name, such as members.updated.
    Type string `json:"type"`
    // CreatedAt is the time when the event was created.
    CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
    // Object references the affected API resource.
    Object EventObject `json:"object"`
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```


<a name="TypedEvent[T].FetchObject"></a>
### func \(TypedEvent\[T\]\) [FetchObject](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/events.go#L69>)

```go
func (e TypedEvent[T]) FetchObject(ctx context.Context) (*T, error)
```

FetchObject retrieves the latest resource using the client that parsed the notification.

The URL must have the SumUp API origin. Its path and query are resolved against the client's configured base URL; URL credentials and fragments are ignored. Requests use the client's authentication and transport, with redirects disabled. API failures return an \*APIError, which may wrap a \*Problem for deleted resources.

<a name="Secret"></a>
## type [Secret](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/secret/secret.go#L17-L19>)

Secret wraps sensitive string values like passwords to prevent accidental exposure in logs, debug output, or error messages. The underlying value is kept private and masked when formatted or printed.

```go
type Secret struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/secret/secret.go#L22>)

```go

```

New creates a new Secret from a string value.

<a name="Secret.GoString"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [GoString](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/secret/secret.go#L50>)

```go
func (s Secret) GoString() string
```

GoString returns a masked representation for Go's %\#v format. This prevents exposure when using fmt.Printf with the %\#v verb.

<a name="Secret.MarshalJSON"></a>
### func \(Secret\) [MarshalJSON](<https://github.com/sumup/sumup-go/blob/main/secret/secret.go#L39>)

```go
func (s Secret) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalJSON serializes the secret as a plain JSON string. The actual value is preserved during serialization for API communication.

```go
func (s Secret) String() string
```



Value returns the underlying secret value as a string.

# full

```go
import "github.com/sumup/sumup-go/example/full"
```

This example demonstrates a complete checkout flow with the SumUp payment widget.

Basic steps: 1. Create a checkout for the desired amount using the SDK 2. Initiate the payment widget with the checkout ID

Prerequisites: \- SUMUP\_API\_KEY environment variable with your SumUp API key \- SUMUP\_MERCHANT\_CODE environment variable with your merchant code

To run:

```
export SUMUP_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export SUMUP_MERCHANT_CODE="your-merchant-code"
go run main.go
```

Then open http://localhost:8080 in your browser.

# oauth2

```go
import "github.com/sumup/sumup-go/example/oauth2"
```

OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with SumUp

This example walks your through the steps necessary to implement OAuth 2.0 \(\<https://oauth.net/\>\) in case you are building a software for other people to use.

To get started, you will need your client credentials. If you don't have any yet, you can create them in the \[Developer Settings\]\(https://me.sumup.com/en-us/settings/oauth2-applications\).

Your credentials need to be configured with the correct redirect URI, that's the URI the user will get redirected to once they authenticate and authorize your application. For development, you might want to use for example \`http://localhost:8080/callback\`. In production, you would redirect the user back to your host, e.g. \`https://example.com/callback\`.
